original_question: Let X and X' be hyperkahler manifolds of the same dimension. If there is a Hodge isometry lambda: H^2(X, Z) -> H^2(X', Z), determine what geometric relationship between X and X' follows, and whether one can force X and X' to be isomorphic by requiring lambda to preserve additional structure beyond the Hodge structure itself.
target_in_paper: Question 2 in §2.3 ("The period map"): the higher-dimensional Torelli question for compact hyperkähler manifolds.
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the paper's target very closely: it assumes two hyperkähler manifolds of the same dimension, asks about the consequence of a Hodge isometry on H^2(X,Z), and separately asks whether preserving additional structure can force X and X' to be isomorphic. Those are exactly the two parts of Beauville's Question 2.
missing_details: The paper is about compact hyperkähler manifolds in Beauville's sense (irreducible holomorphic symplectic manifolds), not arbitrary noncompact hyperkähler manifolds.

The Hodge isometry is an integral isometry of the second cohomology lattices equipped with the Beauville-Bogomolov quadratic forms q_X and q_X', and it must induce an isomorphism of Hodge structures on H^2.
The question is posed as an open Torelli-type problem: the paper does not state a definitive geometric conclusion, so "determine" should be softened to "what can one conclude" or "what can one say."
The intended context is the missing higher-dimensional analogue of global Torelli: local Torelli and surjectivity of the period map are known, but the global statement fails in naive form.

The phrase "beyond the Hodge structure itself" is slightly imprecise here, because the paper's hypothesis already includes an isometry as well as the Hodge structure; Beauville asks more neutrally whether lambda should preserve "some extra structure."

To be fully paper-faithful, one should not build in a specific extra structure such as a polarization or Kähler cone unless stated separately; Beauville deliberately leaves the extra structure unspecified.
Nearby context shows that even equal periods (with suitable markings), and even the polarized analogue, do not suffice in general because of Namikawa's generalized Kummer counterexample.
refined_question: Let X and X' be compact hyperkähler (irreducible holomorphic symplectic) manifolds of the same complex dimension. Suppose there exists a Hodge isometry lambda:(H^2(X,Z),q_X) -> (H^2(X',Z),q_X'), i.e. an integral isometry for the Beauville-Bogomolov forms that respects the Hodge decompositions on H^2(-,C). What can one conclude about the geometric relation between X and X'? In particular, can one force X and X' to be isomorphic by requiring that lambda preserve some additional structure?
justification: The draft is essentially a paraphrase of Beauville's Question 2. In the surrounding discussion, Beauville first recalls the K3 case, where global Torelli says that a Hodge isometry on H^2 characterizes isomorphism, then introduces the higher-dimensional period map and states that only local Torelli and surjectivity are known there. He immediately explains why the naive higher-dimensional global Torelli statement fails: any birational map induces a Hodge isometry, and Namikawa's example shows that two generalized Kummer manifolds can have the same period with appropriate markings without being bimeromorphic. He therefore asks exactly what a Hodge isometry implies for two same-dimensional hyperkähler manifolds, and whether adding further preserved structure can recover isomorphism. The next paragraph notes partial progress by Markman and Verbitsky, confirming that this is the precise nearby problem your draft is aiming at.

Discussion following Question 2 (polarized analogue; partial answers of Markman and Verbitsky)
